edges.description: Without zonular tension the lens relaxes into a small spherical shape.
A deficient zonule also fails to anchor the lens, allowing it to displace.
A small, thick, forward-sitting lens crowds the anterior chamber and obstructs aqueous flow through the pupil.
An anteriorly displaced lens obstructs the pupil directly.
Obstructed aqueous egress raises intraocular pressure.
Sustained pressure elevation drives retinal ganglion cell death.
Ganglion cell loss manifests as optic nerve degeneration and progressive visual field loss.

nodes.description: The convergent lesion is a sparse and disorganized fibrillin microfibril network in the extracellular matrix. Because fibrillin microfibrils are both a structural template for elastic fibres and a reservoir controlling TGF-beta-superfamily growth factor bioavailability, the consequences are simultaneously mechanical and signalling.

evidence.reference_title: ADAMTS10-mediated tissue disruption in Weill-Marchesani syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Fibrillin microfibrils are extracellular matrix assemblies that form the template for elastic fibres, endow blood vessels, skin and other elastic tissues with extensible properties. They also regulate the bioavailability of potent growth factors of the TGF-β superfamily.

evidence.reference_title: LTBP2 mutations cause Weill-Marchesani and Weill-Marchesani-like syndrome and affect disruptions in the extracellular matrix.
evidence.snippet: Light, fluorescent, and electron microscopy evidenced disruptions of the microfibrillar network in the ECM of the proband's skin.

nodes.description: In the ADAMTS10 mouse model, growth plate zones are perturbed with altered cell proliferation, GDF8 and BMP growth factor genes are downregulated, and SMAD1/5/8 signalling falls while p38 MAPK signalling rises. This is the signalling arm through which a structural matrix defect becomes a growth and muscle phenotype, and it is the point at which WMS diverges from the TGF-beta-overactivation logic of Marfan syndrome.

nodes.description: The dominant arm acts on fibrillin-1 itself, and LTBP2 acts as a microfibril-associated binding protein. Because all four WMS genes encode secreted extracellular matrix proteins that build or decorate the same fibrillin microfibril, the four genotypes are clinically indistinguishable despite differing inheritance.

evidence.snippet: WMS can be caused by recessive mutations in ADAMTS10 (WMS 1), ADAMTS17 (WMS 4), or LTBP2 (WMS 3), or by dominant mutations in fibrillin-1 (FBN1) (WMS 2); all genes encode secreted extracellular matrix (ECM) proteins.

evidence.snippet: Autosomal recessive and autosomal dominant forms of Weill-Marchesani syndrome, an inherited connective tissue disorder, are caused by mutations in ADAMTS10 (encoding a secreted metalloprotease) and FBN1 (encoding fibrillin-1, which forms tissue microfibrils), respectively, yet they are clinically indistinguishable.

evidence.reference_title: LTBP2 mutations cause Weill-Marchesani and Weill-Marchesani-like syndrome and affect disruptions in the extracellular matrix.
evidence.snippet: Latent transforming growth factor (TGF) beta-binding protein 2 (LTBP2) is an extracellular matrix (ECM) protein that associates with fibrillin-1 containing microfibrils.

nodes.description: ADAMTS10 and ADAMTS17 are secreted metalloproteases that bind fibrillin-1 directly and promote its deposition. ADAMTS10 accelerates microfibril biogenesis when supplied exogenously, and is a poor fibrillinase because its zymogen resists furin activation, so its role is assembly rather than turnover. Loss-of-function variants therefore subtract a microfibril builder rather than releasing a protease brake.

nodes.description: This node makes the organ-specific substitution explicit. The conserved glaucoma module places trabecular meshwork extracellular matrix dysfunction at this position; in WMS the obstruction to aqueous outflow is instead purely anatomical, a microspherophakic or subluxated lens blocking the pupil and closing the angle, with a structurally normal trabecular meshwork. It also explains the paradoxical pharmacology, since miotics thicken the lens and worsen block while mydriatics can dislocate the lens forward.
